description:
AI student and UI/UX designer taking on Martian Map: a tool a Mars astronaut could use to plan a Marswalk. Real NASA images and elevation data, computer vision to spot rocks and steep slopes, and a safe route to science targets. I bring design, front-end and AI/ML, plus a clear plan already underway. Fully online, join from anywhere. Beginners welcome!

Looking for: Mars/geology fans (no coding needed), Python/GIS or computer vision, and video/storytelling for the demo.
summary: Marswalk Planner is a web map that helps plan a safe Mars EVA (Marswalk) in Gale Crater, at the foot of Mount Sharp. It layers three kinds of NASA data: HiRISE optical imagery, topography from the HiRISE elevation model (slope and hillshade), and THEMIS thermal inertia, which indicates firm rock versus soft dust. Slope is classified as safe, caution or no-go, and a least-cost path algorithm plans one continuous loop from a start point through three science stops and back, never entering no-go terrain. A safety slider lets the user change the maximum slope limit and see the route, distance and maximum slope update, because the real suit limit on Mars is uncertain. The panel also shows total distance, farthest distance from the start, estimated walking time and an elevation profile colored by slope class. Astronaut safety comes first: steep terrain is blocked with a safety buffer, and every assumption is labeled and configurable. There is no machine learning, only transparent slope math and shortest-path routing, so every result can be checked. The code is open source.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

The planner takes a 2 x 2 km crop of Gale Crater (Mount Sharp boxwork area) and lets a user view it as toggleable layers: HiRISE orthoimage (optical), hillshade and slope classes derived from the HiRISE DTM (topographic), THEMIS thermal inertia (thermal), and possible boulders detected from shadows in the 0.25 m HiRISE image (not validated). It plans a closed loop from a base through three science stops and back, avoiding no-go slopes and steering away from boulder-dense ground. The panel shows total distance, max slope, farthest distance from base, estimated walking time, boulders within 5 m of the route, per-leg stats, and a slope-colored elevation profile. A slider lets the user change the max-slope limit (10 to 20 degrees); where no safe loop exists, the tool shows the gentlest possible loop and labels it as exceeding the limit.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Slope is computed from the 1 m HiRISE DTM using pixel size in metres.

2. Cells are classed safe (<=15 deg), caution (15-20 deg) or no-go (>20 deg, plus a 1-pixel safety buffer).

3. Possible boulders are found in the 0.25 m HiRISE image with classical image processing (shadow thresholding, morphology, connected components). No machine learning.

4. A cost map penalizes steeper ground and boulder density, and blocks no-go cells.

5. skimage's route_through_array finds the cheapest route between stops.

6. THEMIS thermal inertia is read remotely for only our window and resampled to the map grid (coarse, 100 m/pixel).

7. A static Leaflet web map shows all layers and results.

SAFETY AND HONESTY

- Slope limits are lunar figures (NASA HLS suited-walking requirement, 20 deg; a 15 deg cap from a lunar traverse study) used as assumptions because we found no validated Mars suit limit. They are configurable.

- Walking speed (0.8 m/s) is an assumed value, not validated.

- Science stops are illustrative targets, not mission-verified.

- Boulder detections are shadow-based candidates, not field-validated.

- HiRISE DTMs can contain artifacts; we checked slopes against the hillshade.

- THEMIS is coarse (100 m/pixel), so it is a context layer, not a fine-scale hazard map.

TOOLS

Python, NumPy, rasterio/GDAL, scikit-image, Matplotlib, Pillow, Leaflet, HTML/JavaScript. No machine learning.

LINKS

Live map: https://minna-chouit.github.io/mars-route/

Code: https://github.com/minna-chouit/mars-route

IMPACT

A transparent, adjustable planning aid for choosing safe walking routes when the exact safety limits are still uncertain.

USE OF AI

AI tools (Google Antigravity with Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude) helped write the code and this text. Demo voiceover generated with ElevenLabs. Code was developed with AI assistance (Google Antigravity/Gemini and Claude). The team directed the work and reviewed the outputs.
